areas.name: Jakarta from above
areas.description: DKI Jakarta from Tanjung Priok to Lebak Bulus. Buildings appear from zoom 12; at this height the rivers, rail and the north coast carry the city.

areas.name: Sudirman–Thamrin
areas.description: The tower spine from Bundaran HI south to SCBD along the MRT North–South line: Autograph Tower, Wisma 46 and the Thamrin offices.

areas.name: Kuningan
areas.description: The second business district along Jalan H.R. Rasuna Said, with Gama Tower and the LRT Jabodebek viaduct.

areas.name: Medan Merdeka
areas.description: Monumen Nasional in its square, with Istiqlal Mosque and Jakarta Cathedral facing each other across the street to the north-east.

areas.name: Kota Tua
areas.description: The Dutch colonial core around Taman Fatahillah, the Kali Besar canal and Jakarta Kota station.

areas.name: Glodok
areas.description: Jakarta's Chinatown south of Kota: dense ruko shophouses, Petak Sembilan market and the temples off Jalan Kemenangan.

areas.name: Senayan
areas.description: The 1962 Asian Games sports complex and the parliament, beside the Senayan office towers and the MRT.

areas.name: MRT North–South line
areas.description: The southern end of MRT Jakarta at Lebak Bulus, where the elevated section begins its run north along Fatmawati.

areas.name: Tanjung Priok
areas.description: Indonesia's busiest container port and its KRL terminus, on the north coast.

areas.name: Muara Baru and Pluit
areas.description: Fishing port, reservoirs and the coastal sea wall in the part of the city where land subsidence is fastest. The atlas shows no subsidence data; read this as a place to inspect with the satellite water layer.

areas.name: Pantai Indah Kapuk
areas.description: Planned estates and reclaimed islands on the north-west coast beside the Muara Angke mangroves.

areas.name: Kelapa Gading
areas.description: A dense mid-rise suburb in North Jakarta with the LRT Jakarta line along its eastern edge.
